title: The p-adic section conjecture
main_claim: For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve X of genus at least 2 over a finite extension k/Q_p, the map X(k) -> Sec(X/k) is bijective (Thm 1.1). The key input is Thm 1.2: at every rank-one norm on k(X) extending |.|_p, K^sep lies in the completion of the universal étale field K~, so decomposition groups in G_K and in Pi_X agree. Combined with Pop–Stix localization, Koenigsmann's birational theorem and a two-henselian-valuation contradiction, this rules out rank-one localizations, and the type-2h case gives point sections. The global corollaries assume finite-cover descent equals C(K) (via Harari–Stix, Stix, Stoll).

issues.description: Two steps lean on external theorems that I could not check against the sources. The collar argument needs Mochizuki–Tsujimura Thm A and Prop 2.4(iv) to give a single finite étale cover whose stable model maps to an arbitrary prescribed semistable model (blown up at the branch sections). The stable-edge argument needs ABBR Thm 7.7 to lift tame metrized-complex coverings, including loop edges, with exact preimages of the skeleton and vertex set. If either result is weaker than stated (for example, it only dominates individual components, or it needs strongly semistable vertex sets), the argument would need adjusting; loops can at least be handled by subdividing. Given the citations as stated, the internal logic is sound.
issues.evidence: Lemma 4.3 proof: 'The RNS theorem, applied with the set of all primes, and its model-domination consequence [MT, Theorem A and Proposition 2.4(iv)] give ... a finite étale cover whose stable model maps to C'.

issues.location: Lemma 7.2 / surjectivity proof: Koenigsmann Prop 2.4(2), Pop–Stix Thm 26
issues.description: The deduction cites Koenigsmann's birational p-adic section theorem (a section of G_K->G_k lands in the decomposition group of a prolongation of ord_a for some a in X(k)) and Pop–Stix's valuative localization. The way they are used matches their known content, but I could not check the preprint numbering or the exact hypotheses here.
issues.evidence: 'The birational section theorem of Koenigsmann places the entire image of s-hat also in the decomposition group of a prolongation of ord_a for some a in X(k)'.

coverage: I read every section (1–8) in full. Checked in detail: Lemma 3.1, local normal form t=z^e including the wild case (root condition v > v_p(e)+1/(p-1)). Prop 3.2 patching: the open cover, the overlap equal to g^{-1}(A_b), splitting of Z^e - t with comaximal factors, GAGA gluing, and the role of roots on every sheet. Lemma 3.3: transfer of the H-valued point. Lemma 3.4 on horizontal indices. Lemma 4.1 annular units. Lemma 4.2: the cyclic cover ramified at P,Q via the divisor P-Q+l·E, Riemann–Hurwitz, harmonicity, the separating-edge reduction, stability count 2N-1 < 3N. Lemma 4.3: the irrational-level argument that the preimage lies in source node annuli, and compactness. Lemma 5.1: division roots through the lattice (torsion-freeness). Prop 5.2: the divisor of T(T-1)/(T-alpha), genus l-1, semistable model with two P^1 components and l edges of length a, slope-1 character for e_j - e_j', Laurent bounds |h| <= p^{-min(s,a-s)}, and log/exp convergence with D > v_p(m)+1/(p-1). Sec. 6: pullback via T = t_b/beta, collar placement inside B_b, l-indices preserved, normality giving F in H. Sec. 7: decomposition-group isomorphism; the explicit two-valuation square-root construction (checked v_1(q_r/d - 1) and v_2(q_r - 1) → ∞); rank and type-2h classification and rationality of a; Kummer/Jacobian injectivity. Sec. 8: skimmed. It is logically conditional on the cited descent results. I did not check external citations against their sources.
